body:
Thanks @simin-yuan! We reviewed `skill-lineage` at `554a951a`. It watches skill writes and keeps a tamper-evident, hash-only record of which session sources (user text, tool results, skills read) each new skill version drew on. The code is clean: no network, no credentials, hashes only, and it never blocks a tool call. One availability bug holds it.

Before it can list:

1. **The e-mail regex is quadratic on hostile input** ([textfeat.py:20](https://github.com/simin-yuan/hermes-skill-lineage/blob/554a951a49489284ad0592ee7916dc2d5b16dd8a/skill_lineage/textfeat.py#L20-L20)). `anchor_strings` ([textfeat.py:80](https://github.com/simin-yuan/hermes-skill-lineage/blob/554a951a49489284ad0592ee7916dc2d5b16dd8a/skill_lineage/textfeat.py#L80-L80)) runs it on every tool result inside `post_tool_call` ([hooks.py:150-152](https://github.com/simin-yuan/hermes-skill-lineage/blob/554a951a49489284ad0592ee7916dc2d5b16dd8a/skill_lineage/hooks.py#L150-L152), [:172](https://github.com/simin-yuan/hermes-skill-lineage/blob/554a951a49489284ad0592ee7916dc2d5b16dd8a/skill_lineage/hooks.py#L172-L172)), and results are capped at 2 MB. We timed the pattern alone: 40 KB of `"a."` takes about 2 s, 200 KB about 51 s, and a 2 MB page would run for over an hour. Python's `re` holds the GIL in one call, so Hermes' hook timeout can't interrupt it, and a prompt-injected web page or file can freeze the agent's turn. A bounded pattern such as `(?<![\w.+-])[\w.+-]{1,64}@[\w-]+(?:\.[\w-]+)+\b` runs 2 MB in about 0.02 s here and still matches `bob.smith+x@example.co.uk`. Please add a timing test that feeds `anchor_strings` `"a." * 1_000_000` plus a one-line pathological input for each pattern.

Recommended, not blocking:
- [skills.py:27-29](https://github.com/simin-yuan/hermes-skill-lineage/blob/554a951a49489284ad0592ee7916dc2d5b16dd8a/skill_lineage/skills.py#L27-L29) reads `HERMES_HOME` from the environment. When one Hermes process serves several profiles, that is the launch profile's home, so writes in another profile's session go unrecorded. `hermes_constants.get_hermes_home()` is profile-aware.

We'll add a disclosure line at merge.

Push the fix, re-pin `sha:` here and comment when it's in; we'll review the delta from `554a951a`.
